<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:province_mapping_certificate}
Let $G_t,\widetilde G_t\ge0$ denote the structural loading scores from the
unknown balanced bus-level injections and the declared reconstruction,
respectively, with $w^0\in\mathcal W^K_{nyd}$. If the branch-stress
aggregator is one-Lipschitz, the declared mass envelope is valid, and the
oracle values are positive, then
\begin{equation}
\rho_K(w^0;G)\ge\left[\frac{\widetilde\rho_K(w^0)V^\star_K(\widetilde G)-E_0}
{V^\star_K(\widetilde G)+E_K}\right]_+,
\label{eq:province_mapping_bound}
\end{equation}
Hence the product is
aggregation-robust at threshold $\rho_{\mathrm{PTDF}}$ whenever the
right-hand side of \eqref{eq:province_mapping_bound} is at least that threshold.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- ieeeproof-1: body_md -->
Within-province PTDF dispersion and the mass envelope imply
$|G_t-\widetilde G_t|\le\epsilon_t$. Summing over the submitted calendar
shows that its value can decrease by at most $E_0$. Maximizing over the
admissible product domain shows that the oracle value can increase by at most
$E_K$. Combining these bounds yields
\eqref{eq:province_mapping_bound}; the complete derivation is given in the
accompanying technical report \cite{kryeziu2026report}.
<!-- end ieeeproof-1 -->
